body:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT - shared-gpu-usw2 pool p99 latency > SLO (streaming stalls). auto-page to on-call. link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/6843215678 :rotating_light:

alice: Paging oncall — I saw the page. joining.

ben: I’m oncall, grabbing context. which customers are impacted?

incident-bot: Affected routes: /v1/stream (us-west-2). p95 220ms -> 1.1s, p99 1.9s -> 6.8s. error rate steady. spike started 6843215600, peaked 6843216400. KV cache hit rate dropped 35%.

alice: Thanks — initial hypothesis: noisy tenant causing IO / cgroup saturation on shared GPU hosts. I’m pulling host metrics.

ryan: FYI eng-runtime — we saw a similar pattern last month with large embedding batch jobs overflowing device DMA and causing stall at tail.

julie: Support: two customers (acme-inc, quickchat) reported slow streaming responses ~20m ago. I’ve opened customer-facing notes and set expected ETA 30m.

ben: I’m running `kubectl get pods -n inference -l pool=shared-usw2 -o wide` to identify hot tenants.

ben: quick snippet from host dstat logs:
```
GPU0: util 92% mem 78% io_wait 45% write_kb/s 120MB/s
cgroup_writeback: host1 98% saturate
process: tenant=acct-1123 cmd=embed-batch
```

alice: Looks like acct-1123 has sustained heavy writeback on host1 and is pushing cgroup IO. I’m going to throttle that tenant at the scheduler level to reduce IO pressure. Will also move latency-critical tenants off that host.

mike: If we throttle, can we avoid evicting? Need to keep streaming sessions alive. Suggest set soft throttling (rate-limit) and enable aggressive batching fallback for the noisy tenant.

ben: Applying throttle: `redwoodctl tenant throttle acct-1123 --cpu=0.5 --io=0.3 --duration=15m`

incident-bot: ACTION logged: throttle applied to acct-1123 by ben at 6843216820.

ryan: I’m starting live-migrate of two high-latency sessions (acme-inc) to dedicated hosts in the same region. Command: `redwoodctl migrate-session ses_9a8b --target=dedicated-usw2-2`

julie: Notifying affected customers: support note updated — "We’re seeing elevated latency on streaming responses in US-West-2; engineering is mitigating. No data loss. ETA 30m." :email:

alice: After throttle, p95 dropped to 380ms, p99 to 1.2s — still above target but improving. KV cache miss still elevated; possible cache contamination from tenant.

ben: Running `kv-cache stats --pool shared-usw2` shows acct-1123 had 52% of recent prefixes in cache. Kicking a partial eviction for that tenant.

ben: `kv-cache evict --tenant acct-1123 --percent 60` — initiated.

incident-bot: KV eviction started at 6843217001.

mike: Monitoring streams for stalls. If stalls persist, we should enable fallback streaming encoder to lower memory pressure.

ryan: Also raising host-level cgroup limits temporarily for high-priority tenants while we finalize migrations: `cgset -r blkio.weight=800` on host2 for SLO tenants.

alice: Quick customer impact estimate: ~7% of streaming requests p99 > SLO during peak, mostly for affected tenants. No 5xx spike.

julie: Support: Acme has acknowledged and appreciates the update. They asked if we can ensure dedicated capacity next week — noted.

ben: Post-mitigation numbers: p95 120ms, p99 280ms for /v1/stream in us-west-2. KV miss rate returning to baseline. Good.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations successful, moving to monitoring. Runbook step: continue 30m observation, then schedule tenant follow-up and postmortem.

alice: Handing off to next on-call: @ryan — keep an eye for 1hr. I’ll create a short postmortem draft and add immediate action items (tenant isolation policy, autoscaling buffer for shared pools, improved cache partitioning).

ryan: Taking over. Noted actions. I’ll also add an alert to detect high single-tenant KV cache occupancy (>40%) earlier.

julie: Support will reach out to Acme and QuickChat with root-cause summary once postmortem is ready.

mike: Follow-ups: (1) propose tenant QoS defaults for shared pools; (2) evaluate automated migration thresholds when single-tenant IO > X for Y minutes; (3) add streaming stall graph to main SLO dashboard.

alice: Thanks team. Closing page — will escalate to postmortem in incidents channel if needed. :thumbsup:

support-bot: Customer notes appended for acme-inc, quickchat. Reference incident 6843215678."
